svg.title: Module 06 one-page guide: Memory: Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 06 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
Memory: Working, Episodic, Semantic,
Procedural
A brilliant agent with amnesia is still frustrating to work with.
Part II · Core Capabilities · Week 6 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 7
OPENING CASE
Analysts re-explained competitors, preferred frameworks, and open research threads at the start of every conversation.
After two weeks, usage dropped 60%. The fix: preferences and open threads stored in a vector database keyed by
analyst, retrieved at the start of each session.
Start simple. Add memory stores only when production evidence justifies the
operational cost — not because the architecture diagram looks elegant.
KEY FRAMEWORK
Four types of memory
Working — what the model attends to right now
Episodic — what happened in past sessions
Semantic — facts and knowledge that don't expire
Procedural — routines learned over a deployment's
lifetime
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Differentiate working, episodic, semantic, and
procedural memory
Match vector, keyword/hybrid, graph, and key-value
stores to memory needs
Design write, deduplication, and retention policies
Anticipate long-term failure modes: staleness,
overlap, sensitive data
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
Hybrid search (vector similarity + BM25 keyword) should be your default; most production vector databases support
it natively.
A user who asks about the same company in ten sessions over three months leaves ten overlapping summaries. Design
consolidation from day one.
Memory accumulates names, affiliations, and financial data. Retention, tenancy boundaries, and deletion are
requirements, not features.
DISCUSS
→ Which memories should never become prompt context?
→ How should an agent resolve a recalled fact that conflicts with the live system?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 7. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
